publication_endpoint: activation of migration versus post-activation progression speed
core_hypothesis: internal migratory readiness strongly predicts migration activation; after activation, generic movement speed is increasingly decoupled from Durif stage and becomes a target for route/opportunity explanations

primary_cohort.boundary: inference is conditional on evaluable processed migration tracks

boundary_groups.FII: n=17; 16/17 from one project, descriptive boundary only
boundary_groups.silver: coarse stage label; not pooled into ordinal Durif analysis

primary_predictions: advanced capture-time Durif state increases probability and rate of migration activation
advanced stage predicts earlier threshold-defined behavioral onset
post-activation migration speed does not show the same general Durif-stage gradient
within-route barrier/hydrological opportunity should explain progression heterogeneity in independent data

primary_estimands.activation: expert-corrected Durif effect on binary initiation
primary_estimands.progression_speed: Durif effect on source-defined migration speed among activated eels
primary_estimands.external_confirmation: barrier/opportunity effects within one route after activation

falsification: independent data fail to reproduce readiness control of migration activation
post-activation speed shows a strong reproducible Durif gradient after route/design control
independent barrier/hydrological opportunity contributes little to progression
evidence_boundary: Canonical interpretation comes from results/phase_control_canonical_v2.json. Terminal endpoint membership is secondary sensitivity because the source meta-analysis did not estimate escapement success rate.
eog_role: discovery of an extreme resident anchor only

secondary_sensitivity.terminal_endpoint_membership: positive terminal/sea endpoint set only; complement not a validated biological failure state
secondary_sensitivity.direct_phase_or_ratio: retained for audit/sensitivity only because phase-2 binary endpoint is observability dependent
